<!-- pr-reviewer: a65a656713a18935e75678ae604f41fc09edfe6c -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes the STEP import geometry path in `crates/kernel`.

### What looks good

- The recovery path starts only for a STEP record when healing removed edges and the healed gap is above `HEAL_GAP_LIMIT`. Solidcraft keeps the old refusal.
- The unhealed source solid must pass the same checks as the healed solid: the integrity check, a 3D curve on each edge, the endpoint gap limit, and then Solidcore level 2 validation. A level 2 finding refuses the solid.
- The importer now checks the gaps before it calculates volume and area. It polls for cancellation before the rebuild, before level 2 and before the measurement.
- The over-limit refusal now gives the source gap, the limit, the input-record edge index, the vertex, the two edge counts and the healed gap. `over_limit_gap_mm` keeps a small excess visible.
- No `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in the new production code. The location lookup uses `Option` and a fallback text.
- No golden, fixture, dependency, process file or UI change. `docs/decisions/3252-step-short-edge.md` records the decision. The new module has a provenance line. All touched files are below 400 lines (`solidcore_import.rs` 372, `solidcore_step.rs` 283, `record.rs` 200).
- The body has a `Changelog:` line and `Refs #3252` (partial work, the issue stays open). The commit subjects are conventional.

### Results merged with main (locally, macOS arm64)

Trial merge of `a65a65671` with `upstream/main` `6e1805bfd`: no conflicts.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 15 steps, 0 failed.

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| kernel build (`--no-run`) | ok |
| kernel lib | 19 passed |
| heal_import | 4 passed |
| import_corpus | 4 passed |
| machining_mesh | 7 passed |
| solidcraft_hostile | 3 passed |
| solidcraft_import | 7 passed |
| step_agreement | 26 passed |
| step_closed_form | 3 passed |
| step_edge_gap | 6 passed |
| step_import | 3 passed |
| step_short_edge (new) | 4 passed |
| step_short_units | ok |
| step_twisted_flank | 3 passed |
| app feature_edge_g1_join | 5 passed |

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

### Extra suites run

- IMPORTERS (the diff touches `crates/kernel/src/`): `step_agreement` (26 passed), `machining_mesh` (7 passed) and `camcraft-app --test feature_edge_g1_join` (5 passed). All are green.
- TEST DATA: the PR adds and changes no file under `testdata/`. The new suite reads `testdata/models/box.step` and edits it in memory. No new STEP fixture, so no `step_agreement` row is necessary.

### Mutations (run by the reviewer)

All mutations are in `crates/kernel/src/solidcore_step/record.rs`. Each was reverted after its run.

1. Ignore the level 2 validation finding: `refuse_an_unhealed_source_with_an_open_gap_between_curves` is red.
2. Always refuse when the healed gap is above the limit (no recovery): `preserve_short_edge_when_healing_would_make_the_gap_exceed_the_limit` and the two refusal tests are red.
3. Remove the source gap refusal: `refuse_short_edge_model_when_its_source_gap_exceeds_the_limit` is red.

The tests pin each of the three guards.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Notes (not blocking)

- The decision file says that the original topology is used "only if it has a smaller maximum gap". The code does not compare the two gaps directly. The comparison is implied: the healed gap is above the limit and the source gap must be at or below it. Thus the rule holds.
- The body says that the cost and the acceptance rate of the recovery on other production models are not measured, and that the release heavy lanes did not run on this head. The cut gate will run those lanes.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Coordinator: this PR merges after the tag v0.25.0, by the maintainer's standing order of 2026-11-21 ("merge using the recommended option"). The review that this merge relies on is the collaborator `pr-reviewer` marker on head a65a65671 (clean). `cargo xtask merge-plan` puts it in wave 1: no refresh is needed. The PR merges cleanly with `main`. I merge it on head a65a65671. It is a fork PR, so its branch stays.
